title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Competitive Methods - IFB
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When a procurement involves highly standardized commodities where price is the only determining factor for award, which competitive sourcing method is most appropriate?
questions.explain: An Invitation for Bids (IFB) or Invitation to Bid (ITB) is utilized when the specifications are clear, the product is standard, and price is the sole factor in determining the award.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A buyer is awarding an IFB. According to standard procurement principles, the award must be given to the lowest bidder who is both:
questions.explain: In an IFB, the standard standard for award is to the lowest responsive (complied with all bid rules/specs) and responsible (has the capability to perform) bidder.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A bidder submits a response to an IFB for janitorial supplies. Their bid includes a substitute product that does not meet the minimum active ingredient specifications stated in the solicitation. The buyer should deem this bid:
options: Acceptable if it offers cost savings
questions.explain: A bid is 'non-responsive' if it fails to conform in all material respects to the essential requirements, specifications, and terms outlined in the IFB.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When utilizing an IFB, public bid openings are typically required by statute. What is the primary purpose of a public bid opening?
options: To allow vendors to revise their prices after hearing competitors' prices
To evaluate the quality of the products submitted
To provide transparency by publicly declaring the identities of the bidders and their bid amounts
To officially negotiate terms and conditions with the lowest bidder
questions.explain: Public bid openings promote transparency and integrity in the procurement process by making the identity of bidders and their proposed prices a matter of public record immediately.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: During an IFB evaluation, it is discovered that the lowest bidder has filed for bankruptcy and lacks the financial resources to purchase materials required for the project. The buyer will likely reject the bid because the vendor is:
questions.explain: Responsibility assesses whether a vendor has the capacity, financial capability, and integrity to perform the contract. A bankrupt vendor lacking resources would be deemed non-responsible.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: In a competitive sealed bidding (IFB) scenario, what should the buyer do if all received bids exceed the available budget for the project?
options: Award to the lowest bidder and ask the finance department to issue emergency funds
Convert the IFB to a QBS process immediately
Cancel the IFB or seek authorization to negotiate price with the lowest responsive/responsible bidder (if permitted by local law)
Award to a local vendor regardless of price
questions.explain: When all bids exceed the budget, the buyer typically must cancel the solicitation. However, many jurisdictions have provisions allowing negotiation strictly with the lowest bidder to reduce scope and align with budget.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: If two identical low bids are received in response to an IFB, this situation is known as a:
questions.explain: A tie bid occurs when two or more responsive/responsible vendors submit the exact same price. Statutes usually prescribe how to break ties (e.g., preference to in-state vendors or coin toss).
